item_1.notes: [chunk 1/1] NVIDIA Item 1 Business filing (10-K, Feb 2025) extracts focus on SIFI-material entities and relationships. Key findings: (1) SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION: NVIDIA has critical wafer fabrication dependencies on TSMC and Samsung, with memory from SK Hynix, Micron, Samsung, and assembly/test from Hon Hai, Wistron, Fabrinet—all concentrated in Asia-Pacific. This is a severity-3 SUPPLIER_CONCENTRATION risk because manufacturing outsourcing is NVIDIA's core strategy, but regional concentration creates geopolitical and supply-chain disruption exposure. (2) EXECUTION_RISK (severity 5): The January 2025 "AI Diffusion" IFR imposes worldwide licensing requirements on high-performance AI chips (A100, H100, H200, B200, GB200, etc.). NVIDIA states it has not received licenses to ship restricted products to China and "understand[s] that partners and customers have also not received a license." This is cascade-triggering because China is a major market, and the licensing regime is retroactively applied. NVIDIA explicitly states competitive position has been "harmed" and "may be further harmed." (3) CAPEX_ROI_GAP (severity 2): NVIDIA discloses placing "non-cancellable inventory orders for certain product components in advance of our historical lead times, pay premiums, or provide deposits to secure future supply"—typical of supply-constrained periods but signals execution risk if demand shifts or export controls restrict sales. (4) NO INVESTMENTS IN PRIVATE AI LABS OR HIDDEN LEVERAGE DISCLOSED in Item 1 Business section. Note 8 (Non-marketable Equity Securities) would be in Financial Statements—separate task. Competitors named (AMD, Intel, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Broadcom, Arista, Cisco, etc.) are significant but generic competitive disclosure. Automotive OEM ecosystem partnerships mentioned generically but no counterparty-specific concentration risk disclosed in this section.

item_7a.notes: [chunk 1/1] Item 7A (Market Risk) contains interest rate and foreign exchange sensitivity disclosures. No off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, investments, or related-party transactions are disclosed in this section. The text covers: (1) fixed-rate investment portfolio sensitivity ($238M impact from ±0.5% yield curve shift); (2) $8.5B senior Notes outstanding at fixed rate; (3) FX hedging contracts and currency exposure analysis. None of these rise to SIFI-material structural risk (no SPVs, VIEs, circularity, concentration, or leverage opacity). Standard market-risk disclosures do not trigger extraction.

item_9a.notes: [chunk 1/1] Item 9A (Controls & Procedures) contains minimal SIFI-material content. The section is boilerplate compliance disclosure covering: (1) effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures as of Jan 26, 2025; (2) management's assessment of internal control over financial reporting under COSO framework; (3) no material changes in controls during Q4 FY2025; (4) ongoing ERP system upgrade in phases since FY2022; (5) inherent limitations of control systems. Item 9B discloses Rule 10b5-1 trading plan modifications by directors Aarti Shah and John O. Dabiri (immaterial for SIFI analysis). Items 10–14 are standard proxy statement incorporations (director identification, executive officers, audit committee, compensation, related-party transactions, principal auditor fees). The only material counterparty named is PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as NVIDIA's independent registered public accounting firm auditing internal control effectiveness. No customer concentration, supplier dependencies, strategic partnerships, equity investments, acquisitions, SPVs, off-balance-sheet arrangements, or hidden leverage signals are disclosed in this section. The ERP upgrade is routine operational capex with no counterparty specificity or SIFI-material execution risk signal provided."

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/2] KEY FINDINGS FROM NVIDIA FY2025 10-K FINANCIAL STATEMENTS & NOTES:

1. PURCHASE OBLIGATIONS ($45.1B total, $35.7B due FY2026): NVIDIA's total purchase commitments are extreme in scale and front-loaded. $30.8B in inventory/supply/capacity obligations for Blackwell ramp, plus $14.3B in other obligations (including $10.9B multi-year cloud agreements). 79% ($35.7B) falls due in FY2026 alone — a severe execution risk if demand softens or Blackwell volumes disappoint.

2. NON-MARKETABLE EQUITY SECURITIES ($3.387B, up from $1.321B): The portfolio grew 156% YoY driven by $1.309B net additions and $816M unrealized gains. A single unnamed private company generated $565M unrealized gain from a Q4 secondary transaction. The filing does NOT enumerate individual investees in this section (Note 8) — investee names must be sourced from a separate roster/exhibit not included in this filing extract. CIRCULARITY risk: many of these investees are likely also NVIDIA compute customers (e.g., CoreWeave, Lambda, xAI, etc. per prior filings), creating investor-is-also-customer dynamics.

3. EXCESS INVENTORY OBLIGATIONS ($2.095B on balance sheet): $2.0B was already expensed in FY2025 COGS and $2.095B remains accrued, suggesting ongoing demand forecasting challenges at massive scale.

4. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (33% of AR from 2 customers): Two unnamed customers account for 17%+16% of $23.1B AR balance — significant single-customer dependence at hyperscaler scale.

5. PREPAID SUPPLY AGREEMENTS ($5.0B): $3.3B current + $1.7B long-term prepaid supply/capacity — off-P&L economic commitments to contract manufacturers representing potential stranded asset risk.

6. DEBT STRUCTURE: $8.46B long-term unsecured notes, ladder maturity from 2026-2060. No off-balance-sheet SPV/VIE structures were disclosed in this section. Arm acquisition termination cost ($1.4B) already expensed in FY2023.
[chunk 2/2] This filing section (pages 75–87) covers tax notes, segment/geographic data, leases, shareholders' equity, and exhibits. Key SIFI-material findings:

1. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (severity 3): Three unnamed direct customers each ≥11–12% of FY2025 revenue, all in Compute & Networking. Combined ~34% of $130.5B. Hyperscalers (likely Microsoft, Google, Amazon/Meta) are almost certainly behind these anonymous labels — the anonymization itself is a signal.

2. UNCOMMENCED LEASE OBLIGATIONS — $7.6B HIDDEN LEVERAGE (severity 3): NVIDIA has signed but not yet commenced leases totaling $7.6B in future obligations (data centers + offices), with terms up to 15.5 years, expected to commence FY2026–FY2030. These are OFF the current balance sheet (ROU asset not yet recognized). This is a material forward leverage commitment.

3. SINGAPORE BILLING OPACITY (severity 2): 18% of revenue billed through Singapore but <2% actually shipped there. This masks true counterparty identities and geographic risk, complicating sanctions/export-control monitoring.

4. EQUITY INVESTMENT DEFERRED TAX SIGNAL (severity 2): Deferred tax liability on equity investments 4.4x'd from $60M to $264M YoY, implying massive unrealized gains in non-marketable equity portfolio (CoreWeave, xAI, etc. — detailed in Note 8 of earlier sections not present here).

5. DATA CENTER REVENUE = 88% of total ($115.2B / $130.5B) — extreme segment concentration, though this is widely known.

Note: Note 8 (non-marketable equity securities with named investees) was not included in this text excerpt. The deferred tax liability signal above is the only proxy available from this section for the investment portfolio risk.
